chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

When a man performs Hajj with his son and he is young, he should instruct him to recite the Talbiyyah and to perform the Hajj as obligatory. If he is not proficient in reciting the Talbiyyah, it should be recited on his behalf, circumambulation should be performed for him, and prayer should be offered on his behalf.

I asked, 'Is there not for them [the children] what they should slaughter?' He said: 'Slaughter should be offered on behalf of the young ones, and the adults should fast, and the prohibitions that apply to the one in Ihram regarding clothing and perfume should be observed for them. If they kill game, the expiation is upon their father.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj)
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَنْهُ: Prayer offered on behalf of another
key_terms.يُطَافُ بِهِ: Circumambulation performed on behalf of another
key_terms.يُلَبِّيَ: Reciting the Talbiyyah (the declaration of readiness to perform Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a father performing Hajj with his young son regarding prayer, sacrifice, and expiation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the father as the legal guardian (wali) responsible for performing the essential rites of Hajj on behalf of his minor son, including reciting the Talbiyyah and offering the sacrifice. It highlights the practical application of vicarious worship in Shia jurisprudence, where the adult bears the financial and ritual burden until the child reaches maturity, while also assigning liability for game hunting to the father as the one overseeing the child's Ihram.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Musny Al Hanaat, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

When a man performs Hajj with his son and he is young, so he should instruct him that he should exclaim Talbiyya, and necessitate the Hajj (as Obligatory upon himself). So if he is not good in exclaiming Talbiyya, he should exclaim it on his behalf, and he should circumambulate with him, and he should Pray on his behalf’.

I said, ‘Is it not for them what they should be slaughtering?’ Heasws said: ‘He should slaughter on behalf of the young, and the older ones would Fast, and the abstention would be upon them what abstentions are upon the ones in Ihraam, from the clothes, and the perfume. So if he were to kill a prey, (its expiation) would be upon his father’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Muthanna’ al- Hannat from Zurarah who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ’

If a man performs al-Hajj along with his small son, he must instruct him to say Talbiyah and make al-Hajj obligatory. If he cannot say Talbiyah correctly, he (the father) must say it on his behalf, make him to perform Tawaf and perform Salat (prayer) on his behalf.’

I then asked, are they not required to offer al-Hady (sacrifice)?’ He (the Imam) said, ’Sacrifice is required for small ones and fast is required from grown up people, and they must stay away in the state of Ihram from whatever the grown up people must stay away, and if he kills a prey his father must pay the expiation.’”
